title: Home & Residential Services
summary: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and other routing-based trades characterized by high fragmentation, non-discretionary demand, and transition to recurring maintenance revenue.
businessModel: Providing break-fix repair, replacement, and preventative maintenance services to residential homeowners.
revenueModel: Transactional revenue for emergency repairs and high-ticket equipment replacements, layered with recurring revenue from annual maintenance agreements.
costStructure: Technician labor, materials/equipment (e.g., HVAC units, parts), vehicle fleet operations, and local marketing/lead generation.
keyKpis: Cost per Lead / Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
whyPeLikesIt: Extremely fragmented (ideal for roll-ups), non-discretionary demand (the AC must be fixed), insulated from offshoring/Amazon, and massive potential for tech-enabled margin expansion.
investmentThesis: Acquire a strong regional brand, roll up smaller competitors for geographic density, implement modern field service management software (like ServiceTitan), and convert transactional break-fix customers into recurring service agreement members.
diligenceQuestions: What percentage of revenue comes from high-ticket replacements versus lower-margin repairs?
How many active recurring service agreements does the company hold?
Is the company overly reliant on expensive third-party lead generation (e.g., Angi, Yelp)?
operationalIssues: Poor routing and dispatching leading to low 'wrench time' (utilization).
Inconsistent pricing and lack of an organized 'good-better-best' sales presentation in the home.
High technician turnover and an inability to recruit new talent.
valueCreationLevers: M&A for density and cross-selling trades (e.g., adding plumbing to HVAC)
aiOpportunities: AI-driven dispatching to match the most profitable technicians with the highest-probability replacement leads.
Predictive inventory management for truck stock.
Automated customer follow-ups and review generation.
risks: Severe shortage of skilled trade labor.
Supply chain disruptions for major equipment.
Rising digital customer acquisition costs in competitive markets.
hundredDayPlan: Standardize a digital pricing book across all technicians.
Implement daily tracking of technician close rates and average ticket sizes.
Launch a technician recruiting and retention program.
exitReadiness: A massive, sticky base of recurring service agreements.
Fully integrated M&A targets operating under a unified brand and tech stack.
Predictable organic growth driven by a dominant local marketing engine.

articleSections.title: The ServiceTitan Revolution and Field Efficiency
body: The core of value creation in the home services sector is transitioning a 'pen and paper' mom-and-pop shop into a highly systematized, data-driven enterprise. This almost universally begins with the implementation of modern Field Service Management (FSM) software, with ServiceTitan being the industry gold standard. By entirely digitizing dispatch, inventory management, invoicing, and customer history, we eliminate the massive administrative bottlenecks that historically throttled growth in the trades. This technological backbone provides the real-time visibility required to manage a fleet of hundreds of distributed technicians.

The primary operational metric we relentlessly optimize is 'Technician Utilization,' colloquially known as 'Wrench Time.' Every minute a highly paid technician spends driving across town inefficiently, sitting in traffic, or waiting for parts at a local supply house is pure margin destroyed. We implement intelligent, algorithm-driven dispatching—optimizing geographic routes to drastically reduce windshield time. This allows us to increase the number of revenue-generating calls a technician can complete from an average of 3-4 per day to 5-6 per day.

This capacity unlock is perhaps the most powerful lever in the playbook. Moving from 4 to 5 completed calls per day across a fleet of 100 technicians represents a 25% increase in top-line revenue without hiring a single additional frontline employee. Because the fixed costs (the truck, the insurance, the back office) remain static, this incremental revenue drops almost entirely to the bottom line as EBITDA. We expect the Operating Partner to utilize the FSM dashboard daily to enforce routing discipline and eliminate 'labor leakage' in the field.
articleSections.callout: In home services, inventory is time. Maximizing 'wrench time' through digital dispatch is the fastest, most capital-efficient path to massive EBITDA expansion.

articleSections.title: Pricing Discipline and the 'Good-Better-Best' Model
body: Historically, technicians in founder-owned trades businesses priced jobs based on 'gut feel' or outdated, dog-eared physical price books, frequently leaving significant money on the table. We professionalize the in-home sales process by completely decoupling the 'repair service' from the 'replacement sale.' We invest heavily in sales training, teaching technicians to utilize tablet-based, highly visual presentations that offer homeowners tiered 'Good, Better, Best' options for major equipment replacements.

This standardized, consultative presentation dramatically changes consumer psychology. Instead of viewing a $10,000 HVAC replacement as a painful grudge purchase, homeowners frequently opt for higher-efficiency, higher-margin systems when presented with clear ROI on energy savings and frictionless financing options. Consequently, we see dramatic improvements in both the 'Close Rate' (sales conversion) and the 'Average Ticket Size,' often lifting revenue per replacement job by 15-20%.

Simultaneously, we enforce strict margin floors by migrating the business to a fully digital, centrally controlled price book within the FSM software. Technicians no longer have the authority to arbitrarily discount labor rates or parts in the field. By ensuring that every dispatched truck is generating its specifically targeted gross profit per hour, we protect the margin at the unit level. For a $50M regional platform, standardizing pricing discipline and improving the close rate by just 500bps can easily add $3M-$4M in incremental EBITDA.

articleSections.title: The Holy Grail: Recurring Service Agreements
body: Private equity sponsors value predictable, recurring revenue at a massive premium. Therefore, the central strategic thesis in home services is converting volatile, transactional 'break-fix' customers into sticky, recurring 'Maintenance Agreement' members. A homeowner paying $15 to $20 a month for bi-annual HVAC tune-ups or plumbing inspections is highly unlikely to call a competitor when their unit eventually suffers a catastrophic failure. These memberships effectively lock in the customer lifetime value (LTV).

These recurring agreements are the absolute lifeblood of a scaled platform. First, they provide guaranteed 'shoulder season' work, allowing dispatchers to keep technicians busy and fully utilized during the mild spring and fall weather when emergency break-fix demand plummets. Second, they represent a captive, proprietary pipeline for high-margin equipment replacements, as our technicians are the ones continuously evaluating the aging equipment in the home. We incentivize technicians heavily on selling these memberships, building a culture obsessed with recurring revenue.

We track the 'Service Agreement Conversion Rate' religiously, targeting a robust membership base where the recurring revenue alone covers 100% of the platform's fixed overhead costs. When a home services business achieves this milestone, every new emergency repair or replacement installation drops directly to the bottom line as pure profit. At exit, a platform boasting tens of thousands of active maintenance agreements is viewed not as a cyclical trades business, but as a highly predictable, annuity-like asset, commanding top-tier valuation multiples.

articleSections.title: Marketing Dominance and Lowering CAC
body: Local home services markets are fiercely competitive, and relying on expensive third-party lead aggregators (like Yelp, HomeAdvisor, or Angi) severely erodes margins and commoditizes the brand. We build a 'Centralized Marketing Engine' focused on establishing absolute local dominance. This involves aggressively investing in local SEO, highly targeted pay-per-click (PPC) campaigns, and a professionalized, ubiquitous physical brand presence—ensuring that beautifully wrapped trucks and uniformed technicians are highly visible in target neighborhoods.

By executing a roll-up strategy—acquiring smaller local competitors and rebranding them under a single, dominant master brand—we gain massive economies of scale in marketing spend. A $100M platform can afford enterprise-grade digital marketing agencies and sophisticated data analytics that a $5M mom-and-pop simply cannot access. We track 'Cost Per Lead' and 'Customer Acquisition Cost' (CAC) relentlessly, utilizing closed-loop reporting in ServiceTitan to tie marketing spend directly to closed, booked revenue.

This data-driven approach allows the marketing team to reallocate budget daily, shifting spend away from underperforming channels and doubling down on the highest-converting keywords and zip codes. This marketing dominance creates an impenetrable, highly defensible moat around our geographic territory. Ultimately, driving down the blended CAC while simultaneously increasing the Customer LTV (via service agreements) creates an exceptionally highly profitable, self-sustaining growth engine.
